messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: state of 2.3, tagging and Git?
parts:
I'm really confused about where we're at in terms of
2.3 tagging and release and where I should be working now.

* I want to update the release notes for 2.3. Where do I
do this?

* I want to declare Stan C++ 2.3 ready for integration into
CmdStan and PyStan and RStan. Or has that already been done?

* Ideally we'll get Andrew's changes into RStan 2.3 if I can
extract from him what he wants tomorrow (Thursday)

* I just filed an issue for 2.3.0+ that should be for 2.3.0:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/698

Is that easy to fix before the release or is it too late?

For now, I'll just stuff the release notes in a text file
pending instructions on where to commit them.

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] state of 2.3, tagging and Git?
parts:
On Wed, Jun 18, 2014 at 8:03 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
I'm really confused about where we're at in terms of
2.3 tagging and release and where I should be working now.

* I want to update the release notes for 2.3.  Where do I
  do this?

There's a RELEASE-NOTES.txt in Stan. I updated it before tagging.

There's also the release management from within github. Here's the direct link:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/releases/edit/v2.3.0

* I want to declare Stan C++ 2.3 ready for integration into
  CmdStan and PyStan and RStan.  Or has that already been done?

It's already tagged, but I could untag it, fix the couple outstanding bugs first.
I'm thinking stuff like:
- makefile incorrect for Stan tests
- duplicate elapsed time output in CmdStan (which is actually controlled by Stan right now, which needs to be broken out further [not in this release]).

* Ideally we'll get Andrew's changes into RStan 2.3 if I can
  extract from him what he wants tomorrow (Thursday)

* I just filed an issue for 2.3.0+ that should be for 2.3.0:

  https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/698

Is that easy to fix before the release or is it too late?

It'd be easy to untag v2.3.0, then tag after fixing.
None of the interfaces have released, so we're still good to change.


If anyone is morally opposed to that, we can tag v2.3.1 right after, but that seems silly since we haven't announced v2.3.0 publicly and all of the maintainers of the Stan interfaces are on this list.

For now, I'll just stuff the release notes in a text file
pending instructions on where to commit them.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] state of 2.3, tagging and Git?
parts:
OK. That makes sense --- untag and then retag.

All of the Andrew-related fixes will be RStan only.
Those shouldn't hold us up in freezing 2.3.

- Bob

P.S. Here's the new release notes. I probably still forgot
something. The commit log's pretty long since 2.2, which
was mid-February.


v.2.3.0 (18 June 2014)
======================================================================

We had a record number of user-submitted patches for this release.
Thanks to everyone who helped out!

New Features
------------
* user-defined function definitions added to Stan language
* cholesky_corr data type for Cholesky factors of correlation matrices
* a^b syntax for pow(a,b)
* reshaping functions: to_matrix(), to_vector(), to_row_vector(),
to_array_1d(), to_array_2d()
* matrix operations: quad_form_sym() (x' *Sigma * x), QR decompositions
qr_Q(), qr_R()
* densities: Gaussian processes multi_gp_log(), multi_gp(),
and alternative negative binomial parameterization neg_binomial_2()
* random number generator: multi_normal_cholesky_rng()
* sorting: sort_indices_*() for returning indexes sorted by value
* many fixes to I/O for data and inits to check consistency and
report errors
* removed some uses of std::cout where they don't belong
* updated parser for C++11 compatibility (thanks to Rob Goedman)
* added JSON parser to C++ (not exposed through interfaces yet)

New Developer
--------------
* added Marco Inacio as core developer

Optimizations
-------------
* turned off Eigen asserts
* efficiency improvements to posterior analysis print

Documentation
-------------
* Clarified licensing policy for individual code contributions
* Huge numbers of fixes to the documentation, including many
user-contributed patches (thanks!), fixes to parallelization in
CmdStan, Windows install instructions, boundaries for Dirichlet and
Beta, removed suggestion to use floor and ceiling as indices,
vectorized many models, clarified that && doesn't short circuit,
clarified von Mises normalization, updated censoring doc (thanks
to Alexey Stukalov), negative binomial doc enhanced, new references,
new discussion of hierarchical models referencing Betancourt and
Girolami paper, (Avraham Aadler and T Malsburg contributed patches)

Bug Fixes
------------
* fixed bug in lkj density
* fixed bug in Jacobian for corr_matrix data type
* fix cholesky_cov_matrix test code to allow use as parameter
* fixed poisson_rng, neg_binomial_rng
* allow binary operations (e.g., < and >) within range constraints
* support MS Visual Studio 2008
* fixed memory leaks in categorical sampling statement, categorical_log
function, and softmax functions
* removed many compiler warnings
* numerous bug fixes to arithmetic test code conditions and messages,
including calls from
* fixed model crashes when no parameter specified
* fixed template name conflicts for some compiler bugs (thanks Kevin
S. Van Horn)

Code Reorganizations & Updates
------------------------------
* CmdStan is now in its own repository on GitHub: stan-dev/cmdstan
* consolidate and simplify error handling across modules
* pulled functionality from CmdStan command class and PyStan and RStan
into Stan C++
* const correctness for chains (thanks Kevin S. Van Horn)
* generalized some interfaces to allow std::vector as well as Eigen
for compatibility
* generalize some I/O CSV writer capabilities
* optimization output text cleaned up
* integer overflow during I/O now raises informative error messages
